takeaway: Subclavian steal: a compressed subclavian artery draws blood backwards from the vertebral artery to supply the arm, causing fainting and visual disturbances.

lines.text: A 58-year-old man, a smoker, has severe cramp-like pains in his right upper limb.
lines.say: A fifty-eight-year-old man, a smoker, has severe cramp-like pains in his right upper limb.

lines.text: They are particularly strong when the arm is hyperabducted.
He also suffers from attacks of fainting,
and he has disturbances of his vision as well.
Imaging shows a pulsatile swelling compressing his subclavian artery.
Now blood flows backwards in the vertebral artery: retrograde flow.
That blood is redirected to supply the arm.
This is subclavian steal. It robs the vertebrobasilar circulation, causing his fainting and visual symptoms.
lines.say: This is subclavian steal. It robs the vertebro-basilar circulation, causing his fainting and visual symptoms.
